PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

ACCEPTING THE LOSS FROM 5b210dcbb0c8 ON THE USER'S INSTRUCTION, NOT MEASURING AN IMPROVEMENT. That commit ("strip every comment and docstring, keeping only what a tool parses") took this lane from its floor to 2110 over it in one commit: 1481 at 5b210dcbb0c8^, 3591 at 5b210dcbb0c8, unmoved since. A @typedef, @param, @returns and @type is exactly what a tool parses, and the strip removed all four; 56 files were left with a literally empty /** @typedef {{ */. 5d04667fcbbe restored the five pure contract files (-9, and it cleared 12 architecture failures), which is why this banks 3582 rather than 3591. A WHOLESALE RESTORE IS WORSE, MEASURED: putting all 50 restorable typedef blocks back reads 3809, because a restored typedef is then checked against callers whose own annotations are still gone. Recovering the 2110 is a decision about the strip -- re-run it with a rule that keeps the four tags, or leave it -- not a ratchet move. See CLAUDE.md section 4. Stamped at a LOCAL-ONLY commit: nothing is pushed, so a rebase before the push re-orphans this.
